SVRTWC

The National Weather Service in Tucson has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Northeastern Pima County in southeastern Arizona...
Southeastern Pinal County in southeastern Arizona...

* Until 745 PM MST.

* At 658 PM MST, severe thunderstorms were located along a line from
9 miles southwest of Avra Valley to 6 miles south of Davis-Monthan
Air Force Base, moving northeast at 35 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and small hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Tucson, Catalina, Oro Valley, Marana, Oracle, Davis-Monthan Air
Force Base, Casas Adobes, Drexel Heights, Flowing Wells, Tanque
Verde, Saddlebrooke, South Tucson, Avra Valley, Saddlebrooke Ranch,

Interstate 19 between mile markers 53 and 63. Route 79 between mile
markers 92 and 106. Route 86 between mile markers 157 and 171. Route
77 between mile markers 70 and 99. Interstate 10 between mile markers
217 and 277.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. These storms are capable of producing damaging winds.

Wind damage with these storms will occur before any rain or
lightning. Do not wait for the sound of thunder before taking cover.
Seek shelter immediately inside a sturdy structure and stay away from
windows.

properties.areaDesc: Greenville, SC; Pickens, SC
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 10 at 9:43PM EDT until October 11 at 9:30AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northern Greenville County in upstate South Carolina...
Northern Pickens County in upstate South Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 930 AM EDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding of low-lying areas adjacent to streams
and other poor-drainage areas, including farmland, parks,
greenways, boat-access areas, golf courses, underpasses, and
parking lots.  Isolated, shallow flows over roadways is possible.
A few flood-prone, low-water crossings may become impassible.  A
small culvert washout or two is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 932 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated a line of torrential
rainfall quickly moving from south to north across northern
Pickens and Greenville counties.  This rainfall is occurring on
top of saturated soils due to a prolonged period of light to
moderate showers that have occurred over the county since this
morning.  Widespread, storm-total rainfall of the 2.5-3.5 inches
have fallen over the past 12 hours. The rainfall has accumulated
steadily, allowing soils to slowly saturate and runoff to slowly
increase, resulting in steady rises in small streams.  However,
this brief period of torrential rainfall is causing more rapid
rises to develop, including along Eastatoe Creek near Rocky
Bottom and Sunset, Oolenoy River from Sunset to Pumpkintown,
Middle Saluda River from Jones Gap State Park to Cleveland, North
Saluda River above the reservoir and below the reservoir near
Slater- Marietta, and the headwaters of the South, Middle, and
North Tyger rivers from Tigerville to Gowensville.  Isolated to
scattered out-of-bank conditions impacting low-lying areas
adjacent to streams are likely to develop over the next 1-3
hours.

- Additional rounds of showers and thunderstorms may develop over
tonight and the threat will persist through the early morning
hours on Sunday.  These showers and storms will be very efficient
at producing heavy rainfall.  Soils are saturated and streams are
swollen. Therefore, additional heavy rain may quickly create new
areas of flooding and cause previous areas of flooding to
redevelop.  As a result, Flash Flood Warnings may be issued
tonight.  Caution is advised near any stream or other vulnerable
area.  Seek higher ground immediately if heavy rain develops.
Please have a plan in place should flash flooding develop and do
not hesitate to act.  Please heed all evacuation orders from
Emergency Management officials.

- Some locations that may experience flooding include...
Travelers Rest, Slater-Marietta, Tryon, Pleasant Ridge State
Park, Jones Gap State Park, Caesars Head State Park, Table Rock
State Park, Tigerville, Jocassee Gorges, and Keowee Toxaway State
Park.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.The St Johns River at Astor remains in Moderate Flood Stage due to
recent northeast winds and repeated rounds of heavy rainfall across
the basin. River levels are forecast to remain just above Moderate
Flood Stage through this weekend and into next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.0 feet, Water approaches or may enter lowest homes
on or near Wildhog Road and nearby canals. Flooding reaches the
parking lot of the Juno Trail Apartments. Flooding on portions of
Alligator Road and Holiday Road. Lowest lying yards along Blue
Creek are flooded. Roads at Astor Landing Campground and Lake
Dexter Boat Ramp begin to flood. Water enters lower homes closest
to the river on McPherson Lane.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EDT Saturday the stage was 3.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 PM EDT Saturday was 3.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 3.2 feet
just after midnight tonight.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued October 10 at 7:04PM MDT until October 12 at 12:00PM MDT by NWS Billings MT
properties.description:
* WHAT...Periods of wet snow expected. Total snow accumulations
between 2 and 6 inches with locally higher amounts possible. Winds
gusting as high as 40 mph.

* WHERE...Southern Wheatland, Beartooth Foothills, Livingston Area,
Northern Park, and Northern Sweet Grass.

* WHEN...From midnight tonight to noon MDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult, due to areas of slushy or
snowy roads and poor visibility. This includes US-191 from Big
Timber to Judith Gap, I-90 from Big Timber to Livingston, and over
Bozeman Pass. Conditions on I-90 over Bozeman Pass are expected to
become particularly hazardous.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Tree and power line damage is possible where
significant snow accumulation occurs, which may result in power
outages.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. Expect areas of poor
visibility. For the latest road conditions, call 5 1 1.
